# Samebase

> Samebase standardizes web apps on the best stack we have found: code in the user's GitHub
> repository, a Convex backend, and Cloudflare Workers delivery. Once you have found the best
> stack, repeat it. Each new app adds a product, not another system to maintain.

Samebase can create a new app in about a minute or connect an existing GitHub repository without
touching its providers. A connected app can remain GitHub-only or attach Convex and Cloudflare
later. In a monorepo, Samebase derives resource locations from each selected convex.json file and
each Worker's live Workers Builds root.

The Samebase starter's core local workflow runs natively on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Its
repository automation is TypeScript run directly by Node 24, so it does not require Bash or WSL.

The dashboard gives humans one inventory of every repository they connect, its provider resources,
derived locations, current state, direct provider coordinates, and provider or connection repair
actions.
Every Samebase action checks its own authentication. Authentication status is a diagnostic action,
not a preflight.
Inventory reports Samebase-owned workflow state and stable resource IDs. It coordinates explicit
Samebase actions; it is not proof of live provider state. Use provider-native tools to verify
current provider existence, configuration, deployment state, and logs unless an explicit Samebase
action exposes that live read.
Codex and Claude Code can install `samebase@samebase`, which packages the create or connect, local
repository build, and Git-backed hosting workflows. Cursor and other MCP clients can call the same
actions directly.

Apps created through Samebase live in the user's own GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare accounts.
Deleting the Samebase account does not stop a running app. The knowledge is free: anyone can build
the identical stack with no Samebase account.

The `.md` links under Docs return raw markdown, and the same paths without `.md` serve the
HTML pages. Action and operate docs are raw markdown only.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://samebase.com/landing-preview): the best-stack opinion, the connected-app
  inventory, and the four claims: yours, safer, lanes, cheaper
- [The stack](https://samebase.com/docs/the-stack.md): what the app template ships and why each
  piece was chosen
- [Do it yourself](https://samebase.com/docs/do-it-yourself.md): deploy the same stack by hand, for
  $0/month, with no Samebase account
- [Receipts](https://samebase.com/docs/receipts.md): every factual claim with its primary source
  and the date it was last checked
- [Pricing](https://samebase.com/pricing.md): what stays free, what will be metered, and why there
  is no price list yet

## Actions

Every operational action has one contract, and these are the same actions the dashboard buttons run.
Choose an explicit action whose contract matches the required stable IDs, then reread inventory.

- [List Samebase vaults](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/get_user_vaults.md): List the Samebase vaults available to the authenticated user, including attached provider resources.
- [List Cloudflare Workers Builds tokens](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/list_workers_build_tokens.md): List the non-secret Workers Builds token names and UUIDs in the Cloudflare account connected to a Samebase organization, with its available last-used UUID.
- [Create Samebase app](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_repository.md): Create a new Samebase app by starting the managed app provisioning workflow: create the GitHub repository, seed the starter app, provision Convex, and provision Cloudflare.
- [Connect existing repository](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/connect_existing_repository.md): Connect an existing GitHub repository as a Samebase vault and sync its repository tree; Convex and Cloudflare stay unconfigured until explicitly attached.
- [Discover Convex projects](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/discover_convex_projects.md): Discover Convex code locations in a vault's GitHub repository and projects available through the connected Convex team.
- [Discover Cloudflare Workers](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/discover_cloudflare_workers.md): Discover Workers in the vault's stored Cloudflare account and observe which ones are currently connected to this vault's GitHub repository and live Workers Builds roots.
- [Attach Convex projects](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/attach_convex_projects.md): Attach selected existing Convex projects to a vault at discovered repository code locations.
- [Attach Cloudflare Workers](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/attach_cloudflare_workers.md): Attach selected existing Cloudflare Workers to a vault after re-verifying their identities and live GitHub repository roots.
- [Create Cloudflare Worker](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_cloudflare_worker.md): Create and attach a Cloudflare Worker in the vault's stored Cloudflare account, configure Workers Builds for that repository root, and request the first production build.
- [Configure Workers Builds for GitHub](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/configure_workers_builds_for_github.md): Configure the selected Worker's production and preview Workers Builds triggers for the vault's GitHub repository, then start a production build.
- [Rotate Convex deploy keys for Workers Builds](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/rotate_convex_deploy_keys_for_workers_builds.md): Rotate Samebase-named production and preview Convex deploy keys, write them with the readable SAMEBASE_CONVEX_PROJECT marker to both Workers Builds triggers, then start a production build.
- [Retry infrastructure provisioning](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/retry_infrastructure_provisioning.md): Retry a failed managed provisioning run for a Samebase-managed app, resuming from the failed step.
- [Create browser handoff](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_browser_handoff.md): Create a short-lived one-time Samebase browser sign-in URL for the MCP grant's current user. The URL is sensitive and expires quickly.
- [Get authentication status](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/get_authentication_status.md): Read the caller's current Samebase MCP authentication state: account identity, role, access keys, and OAuth token scopes.

## Operate

- [Agent plugin](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/agent-plugin.md): install `samebase@samebase`
  for the building and Git-backed hosting workflows around this action catalog
- [MCP server](https://api.samebase.com/mcp): connect a coding agent over MCP (OAuth happens in the
  browser); the tools are the actions listed above.
- [Production logs](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/production-logs.md): read backend and Worker
  logs provider-direct, with coordinates from get_user_vaults
- [Custom domain](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/custom-domain.md): attach a domain to the
  app's Worker in your own Cloudflare account
